subject: Architecture
title: Afrofuturism in Architecture: Designing African Futures
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Afrofuturism in Architecture: Designing African Futures.

hook.text: African architects are rejecting Western templates and designing buildings rooted in local identity.

buildup.text: David Adjaye, Francis Kéré, and Mariam Kamara draw on African materials, patterns, and climate strategies.

discovery.text: Kéré's school in Burkina Faso uses clay bricks and a raised tin roof to cool classrooms without power.

twist.text: Kéré won the 2022 Pritzker Prize — architecture's highest honor — for buildings made of local mud and labor.

climax.text: Africa's cities are the world's fastest growing. The architecture being built now will define a century.

punchline.text: The future of architecture might not look Western at all.

quiz.question: What material does Francis Kéré famously use in his buildings?
options: Local clay bricks and simple materials
